High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:179113
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 36070 of 2023

Applicant :- Rampal
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- P.H. Vashishtha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri P.H.Vashishtha, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur,
learned Aga-I, for the State.

2.  The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Sessions Trial No.21 of 2018 arising out of Case Crime No.261 of 2017, under Sections 376 and 406 IPC, Police Station Sahabad, District Rampur during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 5.5.2017 against the applicant under Sections 376 and 406 IPC and according to the FIR, after the death of husband of the informant applicant sexually exploited her under the false promise of marriage.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that applicant also misappropriated Rs.One Lac of the informant and refused to perform marriage with her.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that technically this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant as first bail application of applicant was dismissed by this Court due to non-prosecution vide order dated 7.12.2021 passed in Criminal Misc.Bail Application No. 6623 of Rampal vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124199528/
1 2018.

entities.text: Criminal Misc.Bail Application No. 6623 of Rampal vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. He further submtis that on merit bail application of the applicant was never dismissed.

6. He further submits that admittedly the prosecutrix, i.e., informant of the case is a major and married lady and from the FIR and from her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it reflects that she was consenting party.
7.

He further submits that although earlier applicant has been convicted by the trial court in another case under Section 376 IPC but his appeal before this Court is pending and he is on bail in that case.

8. He further submits that applicant is in jail in the present matter since 5.10.2017, i.e., for almost six years and trial of the case could not be concluded till date and even at present it is at the evidence stage.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayerfor bail and submits that applicant is a convicted person and he used to commit offences like rape and earlier also he has been convicted under Section 376 IPC but could not dispute the fact that victim of the present case is a major and married lady and in the present matter applicant is in jail for almost six years.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
11. Although this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant but his first bail application was dismissed for non-prosecution.

12. Further, applicant appears to be a convicted person and earlier he has been convicted under Section 376 IPC and his appeal is pending before this Court but from the perusal of the FIR and the statement of the prosecutrix recorded during investigation it appears that she was major and married lady and it appears that with her consent physical relationship was developed between her and applicant and further applicant in the present matter is in jail since October, 2017, i.e., for almost six years.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, particularly the long incarceration of the applicant for almost six years, in my view, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Rampal be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
Rampal vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124199528/
2
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 18.9.2023 SKM  Rampal vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124199528/
